claims.statement: This page is an agent-only routing map for the documentation tree under openwiki/. It is not published to the public site.
The openwiki/ tree contains exactly 17 public pages under the listed Public Paths (excluding the auto-generated Home at openwiki/index.md) and 2 agent-only pages under openwiki/testing/.

The 17 public pages are: getting-started/installation.md, getting-started/quickstart.md, concepts/how-it-works.md, concepts/citation-alignment.md, concepts/hallucination-detection.md, concepts/fact-verification.md, configuration/citation-config.md, configuration/presets.md, configuration/tokenizers.md, configuration/segmenters.md, integrations/langchain.md, integrations/llamaindex.md, integrations/custom-sources.md, advanced/multi-span-evidence.md, advanced/embedding-retrieval.md, advanced/rust-acceleration.md, advanced/performance-tuning.md (Home at openwiki/index.md is auto-generated and excluded from the 17).

The 2 agent-only pages are openwiki/testing/pytest-markers.md and openwiki/testing/contract-tests.md. They are denser than the public pages, may mention openwiki/ paths, and are never published to the public site.

Public-to-public links use relative paths (for example ../concepts/how-it-works.md). Public pages must never link to openwiki/testing/ or to this routing page, must never use /openwiki/ or openwiki/ prefixes in reader-facing hrefs, and must never use the words wiki, MkDocs, or OpenWiki in prose.

After a successful OpenWiki update, scripts/publish_openwiki_to_docs.py copies the public paths from openwiki/ into docs/. The openwiki/testing/ pages and openwiki/quickstart.md itself are not part of that copy.

Reader or public-page questions route to openwiki/index.md (Home) and the 16 public pages. Pipeline work routes to openwiki/concepts/how-it-works.md. Python/Rust parity work routes to openwiki/testing/contract-tests.md. Optional-dependency test work routes to openwiki/testing/pytest-markers.md.

Public pages must use the install name cite-right and the import package cite_right, address the reader as you, give one H1 followed by a short opening paragraph and ## Title Case sections, put a small runnable example before a long theory dump, and never use the words wiki, MkDocs, or OpenWiki.
Status literals on public pages are exactly "supported", "partial", or "unsupported". The literal is "partial", never "partially_supported". "partial" means low answer coverage or contradiction.

The only allowed measured numbers on public pages are: 50-case pack with no embedder, p50 wall about 12.4ms versus about 175.8ms in 0.3.1 (roughly 14×), spp 81.3% versus 83.4%; RAGTruth test 2,675 answers, false-supported on gold hallucinations about 1.6%, unsupported precision about 14%. Any other latency or quality figure must be omitted.

Openwiki/INSTRUCTIONS.md lists invariants that every public page touching them must preserve: public API align_citations and PreparedCitationCorpus with default supported_answer_coverage=0.6; half-open char_start/char_end with the source.text[char_start:char_end] == evidence equality; default/Rust path uses inverted index with rare-token intersect and Smith-Waterman localization; fallback path leaves inverted_index=None and uses lexical selection; embedder path may add non-index windows that still need Smith-Waterman and retrieval_support is not a Citation; Rust prepare still runs with an embedder when SimpleTokenizer and SimpleSegmenter are in use; contradiction downgrades to "partial" with citations, never "unsupported"; content-word overlap can emit a citation when sequential Smith-Waterman coverage is low; Data2txt field:value gets a second Smith-Waterman pass with gap_score=0.
Agents must not generate a second public tree such as architecture/, operations/, or workflows/. Extra depth for agents belongs under openwiki/testing/ or not at all.
